metadata.title: CrowdStrike’s all-stock bid for Zscaler: deal structure shifts risk to target holders

content.text:
Investing.com -- CrowdStrike's all-stock bid for Zscaler puts the price risk squarely on Zscaler shareholders, and the market is already pricing that in.
Scorecard
All figures as of Nov 24, 2:48 PM EST:
The Spread Tells the Story
-
Terms: Each Zscaler share converts into 1.135 CrowdStrike shares. That implied about $260.41 on Friday, a 34% premium, with an enterprise value near $43.9B. Closing is expected in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028, per Investing.com Read more (Nov 24, 9:43 AM EST).
-
Calculation: At today's $210.10, the offer implies about $238.47 per Zscaler share, roughly 8% below Friday's value. Zscaler trades at $230.75, about 3.2% under that. Since it's all stock, Zscaler holders carry the price risk.
-
Why the market is skeptical: The size is the issue. Both stocks carry flags for high EBITDA multiples in our data, and Zscaler is not profitable on a trailing basis.
The Case for Both Sides
-
Bull view: CrowdStrike reported fiscal Q3 adjusted EPS of $0.34 on revenue of $1.58B, up 28%, beating estimates. Management targets $500M in annual cost savings within 18–24 months and about $1B of revenue synergies within 30 months. Guggenheim upgraded CrowdStrike to Buy, FBN raised its target to $235 and Jefferies kept a $240 target Read more (Nov 24, 2:02 AM EST).
-
Bear view: TD Cowen downgraded Zscaler to Hold, and Freedom Broker cut its Zscaler target to $260 Read more (Nov 24, 12:32 AM EST). Integration at this scale is new for CrowdStrike, and cross-sell gains may be smaller than hoped.
A Rough Day for the AI Complex
The tape adds pressure to the stock-as-currency argument. Nasdaq 100 (NDX) is at 26,184.04, down 2.10%. NVIDIA (NVDA) is down 7.55%, and Anthropic (ANT) is down 8.83%, a deeper fall than the "slightly" in the column. The Monday rally has largely reversed.
